chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who urinated, then performed wudu (ablution), and stood for salat (prayer), then found wetness. He said:
“There is nothing upon him, and he does not perform wudu (ablution) again.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer) he was preparing to perform
key_terms.بَلَلًا: wetness found after urination and wudu
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: no liability or required action is upon him
key_terms.وَلَا يَتَوَضَّأُ: he does not need to perform wudu again

ai.seo_question: If someone finds wetness after urinating and performing wudu, must he repeat his ablution?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who notices wetness after urinating, performing wudu (ablution), and preparing for salat (prayer). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that no consequence is upon him and that he does not need to repeat his wudu.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.147 - Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man who urinates, performs ablution, then stands for prayer and finds wetness.
Imam (as) said: 'There is nothing upon him, and he does not need to perform ablution again.'.
